title: Physics arXiv daily — 8 notable papers from the 28 October 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart; ordering is an inferred notable-paper ranking, not a readership or download ranking. Citation evidence is limited for these recent papers: Semantic Scholar reported zero current citations and zero influential citations for each of the eight selected works at the snapshot.

sections.title: Search for Neutrino-Produced Long-Lived Particles Using the SBND Cosmic Ray Tagger Beam Telescope
sections.abstract: The SBND CRT Beam Telescope dataset enables a search for neutrino-produced long-lived particles decaying to electron–positron pairs; no significant excess is found and 90% confidence limits are set.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report no significant excess and 90% CL upper limits on effective production cross sections of roughly 10⁻³⁷–10⁻³⁹ cm² across 0.3–100 m laboratory decay lengths.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; CRT Beam Telescope data from the Booster Neutrino Beam, corresponding to 2.95×10²⁰ protons on target
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify limited geometric acceptance and reduced event information in the CRT-only configuration as sensitivity limits.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: First beyond-Standard-Model search using this standalone SBND CRT data set, with a concrete decay-length-dependent limit and Fermilab report number FERMILAB-PUB-26-0632-PPD.

sections.title: Measurement of antideuteron and net-Λ number fluctuations at the Large Hadron Collider
sections.abstract: ALICE measures antideuteron–net-Λ number correlations in Pb–Pb collisions to separate correlations associated with hadronization from those associated with antinucleus formation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that the antideuteron–net-Λ correlation and net-Λ second-order cumulant are described by Thermal-FIST statistical hadronization; they argue this supports a nucleosynthesis origin for the antideuteron–antiproton correlation.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ALICE Pb–Pb collision data at √sNN = 5.02 TeV
sections.unique_caveat: The mechanistic interpretation depends on comparisons with statistical-hadronization and coalescence models and is specific to the measured collision system and observables.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A new ALICE collaboration measurement with CERN report number CERN-EP-2026-283, cross-listed between nuclear and experimental high-energy physics, and a targeted observable for a stated model discrepancy.

sections.title: Improving cosmological distance measurements at high redshift using Lyman-Alpha forest BAO reconstruction
sections.abstract: The authors adapt Zel’dovich reconstruction to Lyα-forest BAO and find reduced peak damping and smaller distance-parameter uncertainties in AbacusSummit mocks, including DESI-like masked-survey tests.
sections.claimed_result: In a DESI-like masked mock, reconstruction reduces uncertainties in radial and transverse BAO scaling parameters by about 27% and 10%, respectively; this is a simulation result, not a new DESI measurement.
sections.evidence_type: computational; Lyα mocks built on AbacusSummit N-body simulations, with linear control variates and modeled survey masks
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that mocks omit important observational effects, including instrument response, pixel noise, continuum fitting, finite forest lengths, gaps, and several contaminants; the masked test also assumes perfect continuum knowledge and no radial mask.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Quantified gains on a high-redshift DESI observable, demonstrated across idealized and DESI-like mock configurations; arXiv lists report number MIT-CTP/6133.

sections.title: Weighing dark matter particles with gravitational waves
sections.abstract: The authors forecast that LISA extreme-mass-ratio inspirals in sufficiently dense dark-matter spikes could constrain ultralight dark-matter particle masses through wave-dependent environmental effects on the inspiral.
sections.claimed_result: Using simulated LISA signals and joint inference, the authors forecast order-of-magnitude mass constraints across 10⁻¹⁴–10⁻¹¹ eV for low-mass massive black holes, around 10⁵ solar masses.
sections.evidence_type: forecast/proposal; relativistic inspiral waveforms with modeled accretion and dynamical friction, tested on simulated LISA signals
sections.unique_caveat: The forecast requires sufficiently dense dark-matter spikes and depends on the assumed environmental and binary-waveform models; it is not a detection.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Unusually broad five-category physics/astrophysics cross-listing and a concrete bridge between ultralight-particle physics, dark-matter spike structure, and future millihertz gravitational-wave inference.

sections.title: Improved nonflow control for multiparticle correlators and system-size-dependent evolution from OO to Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC
sections.abstract: The authors validate a nonflow-subtraction method for multiparticle heavy-ion correlators and use it to predict oxygen–oxygen results for comparison with published Pb–Pb measurements.
sections.claimed_result: In tests without collective flow, the authors find their multiplicity-scaled estimator more reliable for nonflow control, then apply it to AMPT predictions for OO collisions at √sNN = 5.36 TeV.
sections.evidence_type: computational; controlled toy model, PYTHIA 8 Angantyr, and AMPT simulations, compared with published ALICE Pb–Pb measurements
sections.unique_caveat: The OO outcomes are model predictions, not reported OO measurements; inference depends on the nonflow subtraction and AMPT modeling.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Four-way cross-listing and a direct methodological response to nonflow biases that can mimic collective signals in small collision systems; the work connects OO predictions to existing Pb–Pb results.

sections.title: Mediated Interactions between Fermi Polarons in the Strongly Interacting Regime
sections.abstract: Zero-temperature quantum Monte Carlo calculations find repulsive mediated interactions between Fermi polarons throughout the polaronic branch and recover RKKY-like behavior for static impurities at weak coupling.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a repulsive Landau interaction at all couplings in the polaronic branch, with short-range universal results insensitive to microscopic interaction details.
sections.evidence_type: computational; zero-temperature quantum Monte Carlo calculations of Fermi polarons and static impurities
sections.unique_caveat: The result is a ground-state calculation within the polaronic branch; comparison to near-resonance experimental trends does not by itself resolve finite-temperature or experimental-system effects.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across quantum gases, atomic physics, and quantum physics; it gives a microscopic benchmark and explicitly addresses a trend seen in prior experiments near resonance.

sections.title: Using Higgs Boson Production in Association with Three Jets via Gluon Fusion at the LHC to Investigate the CP Properties of the Higgs Boson
sections.abstract: The authors calculate Higgs-plus-three-jet production with finite top- and bottom-quark masses and show how jet observables can distinguish CP-mixed couplings from CP eigenstates.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that a counting asymmetry based on a sin(2Φ₂) term isolates interference from CP-mixed couplings, while no CP eigenstate can produce that term.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; perturbative gluon-fusion calculation and kinematic distributions for √s = 13.6 TeV
sections.unique_caveat: These are theoretical predictions; practical sensitivity will depend on backgrounds, detector effects, and available event statistics.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A complete finite-mass calculation across partonic subprocesses and a concrete proposed CP-sensitive azimuthal observable at the LHC’s 13.6 TeV energy.

sections.title: Adaptive Information Mining: Approaching the Quantum Limit of Super-Resolution Imaging
sections.abstract: The authors propose sequential adaptive measurements that steer imaging toward the quantum Fisher-information limit and report lower point-source estimation error than direct imaging in their demonstrations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report point-source estimation error 2–5 times closer to the quantum limit than direct imaging, without prior source-position or brightness knowledge.
sections.evidence_type: computational; adaptive measurement and estimation framework demonstrated in modeled point-source and multi-parameter imaging scenarios
sections.unique_caveat: The reported improvement is a method demonstration; transfer to real instruments will require implementation and robustness tests under experimental noise and calibration errors.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in quantum physics and optics, with a stated quantitative improvement of 2–5× in estimation error relative to direct imaging and extensions to unknown source counts and wavefront distortions.

sections.title: Physics arXiv daily — latest batch: 28 October 2026
sections.text: Eight notable recent papers, led by experimental searches and measurements alongside tools for high-redshift cosmology, dark-matter inference, and quantum systems. Brief agenda: SBND long-lived-particle search, ALICE antinucleus fluctuations, DESI Lyα BAO reconstruction, then gravitational-wave and quantum/collider methods.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
items: Heavy-ion correlations and particle-production mechanisms: ALICE antideuteron–net-Λ measurement (2610.36307) and nonflow/subtraction study with OO predictions (2610.36922); OO prediction is not an independent measurement.
High-redshift cosmology and future gravitational-wave inference: Lyα BAO mock reconstruction (2610.37664) and LISA EMRI dark-matter forecast (2610.37638) are complementary, not the same evidence.
Quantum methods across atoms and imaging: Fermi-polaron QMC (2610.37654) and adaptive super-resolution (2610.37491) link distinct regimes, not a shared experiment.

Collider observables: SBND displaced-decay search (2610.37555) and Higgs-plus-jets CP calculation (2610.37627) offer constraints or discriminating observables; these are isolated signals, not a discovery pattern.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
items: SBND authors identify CRT-only geometric acceptance and limited event information; synthesis: test whether full-detector running and more decay topologies improve sensitivity while controlling backgrounds (2610.37555).

BAO authors note idealized mocks omit instrument response, pixel noise, continuum fitting, forest gaps and contaminants; synthesis: validate with realistic DESI-like mocks/data and systematic variations (2610.37664).

ALICE interpretation uses coalescence and statistical-hadronization models; synthesis: measure complementary species correlations across energies and centralities to test persistence beyond this Pb–Pb observable (2610.36307).
LISA forecast requires sufficiently dense dark-matter spikes; synthesis: vary spike profiles and environmental systematics in waveform injections to test mass identifiability (2610.37638).

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: The clearest new-data results are SBND’s neutrino-produced LLP limits and ALICE’s antideuteron–hyperon correlation. Other notable work provides methods or forecasts whose implications depend on mock realism, modeling, and future instrument sensitivity; none is a discovery claim.

sections.title: Method and sources
sections.text: Daily window 2026-10-28; snapshot 2026-10-30T01:31:30Z. The latest recent-listing batch displayed was 28 October. All 11 configured physics archives were checked (707 archive appearances including cross-lists); eight papers were selected and their arXiv abstracts/version histories verified. Full text for the three leading entries was inspected. Ranking uses concrete results, methods, cross-lists, official report/collaboration metadata, and recency; Semantic Scholar citationCount and influentialCitationCount were zero for each selected paper at the snapshot. A batched arXiv Atom API request was rate-limited; metadata was verified through arXiv web pages. Sources: arXiv recent listings and abstract/full-text pages; Semantic Scholar Graph API.
